requirements.title: The web application shall set a habit's streak to 1 when it is marked done for the first time

vision.paraphrase: Streak initialization on first completion implements automatic streak calculation, delivering the visible momentum goal by showing users they've begun their consecutive-day journey.
Scenario 2 describes the daily check-in experience, and the first completion marks the beginning of the streak journey, starting users at 1 rather than 0.

conops.paraphrase: When a user marks a habit done for the first time, the streak is set to 1, signaling that their consistent effort has begun and is being tracked.

requirements.title: The web application shall increment a habit's streak by 1 when it is marked done on the day immediately following its last completion

vision.paraphrase: Consecutive-day streak incrementing embodies the visible momentum goal, rewarding consistency with an incrementing counter that motivates users to maintain their daily habit.
Scenario 2 shows a returning user checking off a morning run and seeing the streak increment, delivering the dopamine hit that reinforces the habit loop.

conops.paraphrase: The app checks the last completed date and increments the streak when the user marks done on the day after their last completion, recognizing consecutive effort.

requirements.title: The web application shall not change a habit's streak if it is already marked done for today

vision.paraphrase: Idempotency in streak calculation ensures that marking a habit done multiple times in a day doesn't artificially inflate the streak, preserving honest tracking.

conops.paraphrase: If a user accidentally clicks the done-today control twice, the app recognizes the habit is already marked done for today and makes no change to the streak.

requirements.title: The web application shall reset a habit's streak to 1, not increment it, when it is marked done after one or more missed days

vision.paraphrase: Streak reset after missed days enforces the consistency principle that the app rewards consecutive effort, not catch-up; missing a day means starting fresh at 1.
Scenario 3 demonstrates that missing a day breaks the streak, resetting it to 0; this requirement implements that reset when the user resumes after a gap.

conops.paraphrase: When a user returns to mark a habit done after missing days, the streak is reset to 1, honestly reflecting that their consecutive-day chain has been broken and is being restarted.

requirements.title: The web application shall recalculate a habit's streak to 0 on load if a day was missed since its last completion

vision.paraphrase: On-load streak recalculation ensures users always see honest, current streak state without ambiguity, even if they haven't opened the app for several days.
Streak recalculation happens synchronously on load by comparing lastCompletedDate to the current date, maintaining freshness without background processes or polling.

conops.paraphrase: When the app loads, it automatically detects missed days by comparing the stored last completion date to today and recalculates each habit's streak to reflect reality.

requirements.title: The web application shall display each habit's streak count as a visually prominent element on its card

vision.paraphrase: Visible momentum is achieved by making the streak count the most prominent element on each habit card, since it's the primary motivational signal driving user engagement.
The streak count is rendered larger and bolder than the habit name, making it the visual focal point and reinforcing its role as the key metric for user motivation.

conops.paraphrase: The habit card displays the streak count prominently, giving the user immediate visual feedback about their consecutive-day achievement when they check in.

requirements.title: The web application shall render a visually distinct state for a habit marked done today versus one not yet marked done

vision.paraphrase: The design direction calls for a clear visual distinction between done-today and not-done-today states, understandable at a glance, so the user never has to guess whether today's check-in already happened.

conops.paraphrase: When the card visually updates after a check-in, the done state must be immediately and unambiguously distinguishable from the not-done state shown on other habit cards.

requirements.title: The web application shall display a single static hint in a shared location for the habit list explaining that marking done tomorrow continues a streak and a missed day resets it to 1

vision.paraphrase: The MVP scope requires a single streak continuation hint, shown once in a shared location for the whole habit list rather than repeated per card, explaining how to maintain a streak and what triggers a reset to 1.

The design direction mandates the streak-continuation hint as persistent static text rendered once in a shared location for the habit list, providing guidance about streak mechanics without repeating identical text on every card.

conops.paraphrase: The static streak-continuation hint, shown once in its shared location, remains visible during daily check-in, ensuring users understand the mechanics for continuing a streak and the consequences of missed days.

requirements.title: The web application shall render the streak hint as always-visible static text rather than a dismissible popup, toast, or hover-triggered overlay

vision.paraphrase: The design explicitly commits to always-visible static hint text rendered once in a shared location, rejecting dismissible popups, toasts, and hover overlays to maintain a calm, minimalist interface consistent with the product's philosophy.

conops.paraphrase: The hint text must remain constantly present in the page's markup without disappearing based on hover, click, or automatic dismissal, ensuring users can always reference the streak continuation rules.
